title: Microsoft Buyout Emails Hit Copilot, Xbox and Windows Teams With Up to 39 Weeks' Pay
summary:
Microsoft has begun sending voluntary exit offer emails to eligible staff, with fully participating divisions including Copilot, Agents & Platform, AI Experiences, CoreAI, Windows + Devices, Xbox, Finance, Human Resources, Strategy & Transformation, and the Office of the CTO. Cloud + AI and Microsoft AI are partly participating, while Marketing, Commercial Business, Security, Discovery & Quantum, and certain data center and sales roles are excluded from the buyouts.

The packages match Microsoft's standard severance structure, which ran from eight to 39 weeks of base pay based on level and tenure in prior rounds, along with the next two stock vestings and six months of COBRA healthcare coverage. The offer covers about 60,000 employees, or 27% of Microsoft's 223,000 global staff, across the US, Canada, the UK, and India up to internal Level 70, which includes partner-level technical leaders, directors, general managers, and vice presidents. Eligible employees have until the first week of December to accept, with departures set for Dec. 31.

The cost-cutting push comes after Microsoft posted fiscal 2026 records of $331.8 billion in revenue and $133.7 billion in net income, up 31%, while capital expenditures including leases reached 44% of revenue. The company is on track to spend $175 billion on AI infrastructure this year, with quarterly capital expenditure topping $50 billion after jumping 69% to $41 billion last quarter. Microsoft expects fewer workers to take the standard severance deal than its April retirement program, which cost $900 million and was accepted by more than 30% of the 8,750 eligible employees prior to 4,800 job cuts in July.
